page.layout: One printed page, right side of a book opening, with the gutter and binding at left. Running head at top with page number at top left. Main text in one column, cut off at the right edge of the scan. Below the text: a diagram of the moon phases in a circle with Greek inscription, and a sun engraving above it. Running text continues below the diagram. A catchword-like line "Theo" at lower right is a cut-off word.

main_text.p: Eius theorema est hoc: Tempus ab vna con‑iunctione ad alteram est dierum 30. fere, etsi enim motu proprio Luna tantum dies 27. & horas 13. in suo cursu consumat, tamen antequam Luna ad Solem reuertatur, Sol interea integrum signum Zod. emensus est, vt biduo opus habeat Luna, antequam Solem iterum possit assequi & cum eo coniungi.

Sequitur altera affectio Lunæ respectu Solis, nempe Eclipsis quæ est priuatio luminis Solaris mutuatitii in Luna propter diametralem interpositionem terræ inter Solem & Lunam, cuius terræ vmbram Luna subit siue ingreditur.

page.notes: The engraving shows a sun above an arc and a circular diagram of eight moon phases with Greek inscription around the rim (ΣΥΝΟΔΟΣ, ΜΗΝΟΕΙΔΗΣ, ΔΙΧΟΤΟΜΟΣ, ΑΜΦΙΚΥΡΤΟΣ, ΠΑΝΣΕΛΗΝΟΣ); the Greek is not legible enough to copy exactly. Right edge of the text is cut off by the scan, so line ends are incomplete. The final word at lower right is cut off.
